lead: Sioux Falls plumbing deals with deep cold, hard water, basements and fast growth. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Sioux Falls.
risk: frozen pipes, hard water scale and basement plumbing
risk_short: frozen pipes, hard water and basements
why: The Cathedral Historic District, McKennan Park and Pettigrew Heights have homes from the 1890s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines and clay sewer laterals. Southeast and western Sioux Falls are much newer.
Long, cold winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Almost every home has a basement with the water heater, softener and sump pit.
water: Sioux Falls uses wells along the Big Sioux River and aquifers plus Missouri River water from Lewis and Clark Regional Water. The water is hard, and the city partly softens it.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in the Cathedral Historic District, McKennan Park, Pettigrew Heights, All Saints, Whittier, Southeast Sioux Falls and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Sioux Falls Building Services, and plumbers must be licensed by the South Dakota State Plumbing Commission.

faq.q: Do Sioux Falls homes need water softeners?
faq.a: Many do. The water is hard even after the city's partial softening, and scale shortens water heater life. A water test helps size a softener.
